target_customer: Middle class Latin American retail investors, launched in Mexico, who want US dollar brokerage accounts
problem: Traditional institutions in LatAm overcharged and under served middle class savers who wanted US equities and crypto, so access was costly and slow.
business_model: Commission free stock and ETF brokerage with crypto commissions, built on Alpaca's broker API
product_category: Retail brokerage and wealth management platform

founders.name: David Abusaid
education: Tec de Monterrey, BS civil engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 12 years in financial sector consulting in Mexico and Miami; leads administration, legal, partnerships and accounting.

founders.name: George Marvin
education: Tec de Monterrey, BS mechatronics engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page: fintech product management in Berlin and 8 years of consulting.

exit.reason: Cause not public. A Rankia review says Weltio stopped operating and returned all client money on 1 October 2023.

technical_complexity.rationale: Brokerage rails came from Alpaca's API, so the team built onboarding, funding via MXN domestic wire and an app; compliance, not code, was the main difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Built on a third party broker API with zero commission pricing, rivals including Bitso (via Alpaca) could offer the same product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bitso added US stocks in Mexico through Alpaca and Ualá launched US stock investing via DriveWealth, but the source pages are undated so timing relative to Weltio is not established.

market_need_then: The founders cite middle class investors who were overcharged and wanted dollar assets; no spend data is sourced.

branding.domain_note: Used weltio.com; the site did not resolve from this environment.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product focus on fractional shares from $1 and fast account opening, per press

branding.community_and_virality: Raised money from retail backers via Wefunder in 2022, which suggests some community interest, but no brand specific evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Only product press from Alpaca and Crowdfund Insider; no brand coverage, and a Wefunder raise reported as not funded in one source.

outcome_analysis: Weltio launched a US dollar brokerage for Mexican retail investors in 2022, raised about $1.2M by database accounts plus a Wefunder campaign, and announced its Alpaca based platform in January 2023. A Rankia review says it stopped operating and refunded clients in October 2023. No post-mortem or founder statement was found, so the cause of closure is not public.
notes: The $1.2M pre-seed rests on CB Insights alone; Crowdfund Insider says $950K was raised earlier from VCs and angels, and PitchBook gives about $1.25M total. The Wefunder SAFE had a $15M valuation cap and $969,104 raised of a $1.15M goal at report time, while Kingscrowd marks it Not Funded, so the final amount is unknown and the cap is not recorded as a post-money. Closure date rests on one Spanish language review. Competitor pages found were undated, so the list is empty. weltio.com did not resolve.
